questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Preexisting language knowledge and personal connections

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university has most information available on their website and they send informative emails regularly.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international team of Humboldt always answered my emails fast.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied for dormitory through HU and the provided me a place. I would definitely recommeding applying for a dormitory at Humboldt. overall a great experience.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living far from the city center isn't a bad experience, however public transportation can be extremly unreliable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register for the courses with the help of the university portal called Agnes. I think the registration process is very slow and confusing and there was very little information available, so I had to rely on the help of other students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The team responsible for course registration was slow to answer and their answers were sometimes confusing. I had to rely on the help of fellow students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I couldn't register to majority of the courses I wanted to and had to choose different ones.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try contacting the specific professors or teaching assistants holding the specific courses rather than the university administration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took BA level courses that are either german language courses or local culture courses. I took courses on the MA level that are connected to IT.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More loose, less strict however often caotic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: German language courses are a great option to learn the language and understand the german culture while making friends and forming connections.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The German state expects every person living in germany to pay monthly roughly 200DKK for televison and radio, even tho I never used any of those.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Humboldt-University provided me a place in a student dormitory, which made accomodation very cheap compared to other possibilities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lot of cultural events, like meetings and dinners and during the first few month the university hosted free visits to museums and other interesting places.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore Berlin and it's local culture which is full of underground artists and beautiful street art.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Berlin clubs and night life are world famous for a reason and even though Berlin is a huge city there is a lot of nature around.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Extremly easy, people are surprisingly nice and due to the dormitory I could form friendships and personal connections very fast.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you can try conversating in german. Germans are very appritiative if you show interest in their language and culture.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Public transportation is extremly unreliable for me, sometimes rides get cancelled for seemingly no reason and strikes and bomb alarms are almost a daily occurance.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Contrary to popular beleif, germans are very nice and helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for an accomodation as early as possible. I was lucky to receive a place through the university, however finding a place can take more than 3 months.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was a hard but extremly useful and enjoyable experience. In case of a problem try reaching out to fellow students, they can inform you of a solution sometimes faster and in a more reliable manner as the uni administration.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The formation of new friendships and connection and I feel my german greatly improved.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Subjects that are held in german can be extremly challanging and the professors care very little about ur german level, they expect you to understand the lesson completly

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
